answer: Verifiers can test where an agent sits. Each epoch they ping every identity unannounced and log a round-trip delay vector; like the tide, delays shift, so samples repeat for days. Clones on one host, or one island of VMs behind a shared uplink, return near-identical vectors and collapse into one operator, one share. To pass as k agents a farm must rent k distant endpoints with separate clocks and links, paying k times for a flat payout. Yarrow stalks pick verifiers at random, so no probe can be predicted. Honest singletons pay once. Unshareable position is the scarce input.
